images.alt: An automobile stopped near the broken end of the Sunshine Skyway Bridge after the May 9, 1980 collapse.
images.caption_html: A car stopped at the severed Sunshine Skyway roadway after the collapse. The difference between stopping and falling was measured in feet.

images.alt: The bulk carrier Summit Venture beneath the broken Sunshine Skyway Bridge after the collision.
images.caption_html: Summit Venture beneath the severed Sunshine Skyway after striking pier 2S.

images.alt: Diagram showing the Summit Venture collision sequence at the Sunshine Skyway Bridge.
images.caption_html: Collision geometry at the old Sunshine Skyway. By the time the bridge emerged from the rain, the ship had roughly one ship-length left.

images.alt: Automobile halted at the broken end of the Sunshine Skyway after the 1980 collapse.
images.caption_html: A vehicle stopped essentially at the broken end of a roadway that had existed moments earlier.

images.alt: Federal archival view of the collapsed Sunshine Skyway Bridge and Summit Venture after the May 1980 accident.
images.caption_html: The collapsed span and Summit Venture after the accident. Federal archival image.

images.alt: The old Sunshine Skyway wreckage and the later bridge replacement in Tampa Bay.
images.caption_html: The Sunshine Skyway story did not end with replacement. Engineers also changed how the new crossing dealt with vessel impact.
